- **No band matches** (only possible for a driver under 18, whom US-01-BR-04 and the step guard
  already keep out of step 2) → that factor is `100` and a `console.warn` names the table, never
  the age. This is defensive; it changes no AC.
- The function is synchronous and has no side effects other than the warnings.
- **Security.** Nothing changes: no request is added, no permission, router or proxy rule is
  touched, and no step 1 value is sent (US-02-AC-19).
- **Reuse by US-03.** US-03 imports the same `calculateFinalPrice`, the typed step 1 output
  (re-derived as in US-02-Q-17) and the same `CLOCK`. The summary shows the price step 2 showed,
  unless "today" or the plan's published base price changed between the two computations (a
  birthday at midnight, or an editor publishing a new base price before a reload); that is the
  intended behaviour of a recomputed, never-stored price (ADR-0003, US-02-BR-06).

### Consequences

- Good, because it is the smallest change that meets D1: one pure, exhaustively unit-testable

 | The orchestrator misdiagnosed its own shell bug as a product regression | After review fix F07 (Strapi port on `127.0.0.1` only), the orchestrator's e2e run showed 32 failures. It concluded "IPv6 `localhost`" from a test that changed **two** variables at once (explicit env vars and `127.0.0.1`). The real cause was its own command: `env $ENV npx …` in zsh, which does not word-split unquoted variables, so `E2E_BASE_URL` received the whole line. It was caught later, when the same 32-failure pattern reappeared on code that passed elsewhere. A one-variable test (Node 24 `fetch('http://localhost')` against an IPv4-only server returns 200, because `autoSelectFamily` is on) disproved the IPv6 theory. The extra `[::1]` binding (4a82769) is harmless but was not needed. The 403 regression found in the same run was real and was reproduced independently. | Corrected on the record instead of left standing. Rules adopted: **change one variable at a time** when testing a hypothesis, and run e2e only through `scripts/e2e.sh`, which sets the documented env deterministically. |
 | A regression hid a second security bug | The same verification showed a new 403 on AC-03. The root cause was not the relation rule: the two content routers shared one module-level route-config object, which Strapi mutates in place when it assigns scopes. Each router inherited the other's scopes, so a token with only `country.find` could also read form fields. | Fixed by giving each router fresh config objects and keeping the published-only middleware on reads only. Lesson: a failing test with an unexpected status code deserves a root cause, not a retry. Here it exposed a cross-type authorization leak that no test targeted. |
 
+| The orchestrator truncated a control's output and reported a false "clean" | When exporting the US-01 logs, the orchestrator read only the last 8 lines of `scan-secrets.sh` and recorded "one scan exception". The scan had **23** unmarked findings. The logs were merged to `main` in PR #4 with that wrong record. A subagent's later full scan surfaced it. | All 23 were classified by a script that never prints values. 22 are fictitious; one is a real but expired dev-admin JWT whose signing secret was destroyed, which the human accepted as an exception. The logs README carries a correction note. Rules adopted: **never truncate the output of a control** (no `tail`/`head` on scanners, test runners or gates), and the number of findings must match the number recorded before a log is committed (`session-handoff`). |

#

# (e.g. gitleaks), which a team setup should add (see FLOW.md, "team of 5").

#   scan-secrets: allow (<reason>)        e.g. // scan-secrets: allow (fictitious value, negative test)

# (human decision, 2026-11-20).

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

RULES=(
  "github-token|gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}"
  "github-fine-grained-pat|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{50,}"
  "aws-access-key|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}"
  "private-key|-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----"
  "anthropic-key|sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}"
  "openai-key|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{40,}"
  "slack-token|xox[abprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}"
  "jwt|eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}"
  "bearer-header|[Aa]uthorization[\"' :]+Bearer [A-Za-z0-9._-]{20,}"
  "strapi-or-generic-secret-assignment|(API_TOKEN|ADMIN_JWT_SECRET|JWT_SECRET|APP_KEYS|API_TOKEN_SALT|TRANSFER_TOKEN_SALT|ENCRYPTION_KEY)[\"' ]*[=:][\"' ]*[A-Za-z0-9+/=_-]{16,}"
)

if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
  files=("$@")
else
  # Default (the gate): every tracked and untracked, non-ignored file EXCEPT exported session logs.
  # Logs quote fictitious values from the code and are checked separately, with every finding
  # classified and recorded in logs/sessions/README.md (session-handoff skill). Mixing them in
  # would let a new secret in the code hide among the accepted log findings.
  # To scan logs: scripts/scan-secrets.sh $(git ls-files 'logs/sessions/*.jsonl')

### US-02-R1-F01 — Coverage middleware duplicates what the schema can enforce

Evidence: `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/services/entity-validator/index.js`:
- `addMinMax` (around lines 36-45) applies `.min(attr.min)` when
  `attr.required || (Array.isArray(value) && value.length > 0)`.
- For repeatable components, lines 98-109 call it whenever `!options.isDraft`.
- `document-service/entries.js:107-111,141-145` validate create and update with
  `isDraft: !data.publishedAt`, and `publishEntry` (`:159-197`) goes through `createEntry` with
  `publishedAt` set.

So with `"required": true` next to `"min": 1` on `coverages`, Strapi itself rejects `[]` on every
published write (create, update and publish), and drafts stay free. Today the attribute is not
`required`, so an empty array skips `min`. That is why the middleware works, but it is custom
code standing in for a one-word schema change. The comment at `plan-coverages.ts:7-9` ("never in
the Document Service") would also mislead the next maintainer.

Expected: either use the schema (and drop the middleware), or keep the middleware and correct
its comment with the reason the schema option was rejected (for example, an admin UX
difference). Both are acceptable. The human's rule is to keep bespoke backend code to a minimum.

### US-02-R1-F02 — Only the `create` branch of the coverage rule is tested

The test-engineer's note ("asserts that it rejects, not why") is **not** the real gap. The
control test "a plan with a country can be published" proves that the helper's data is otherwise
valid, and Strapi does not reject `[]` for a non-required repeatable (F01 evidence). So removing
the middleware turns the test red, even without a message assertion. The real gap is the other
branches of `plan-coverages.ts:18-25`:
- `publish` of an existing draft that has no coverages. This is the editor's normal path: save a
  draft, then publish.
- `update` with `status: 'published'` and no `coverages` in `data`, which goes through the draft
  lookup.

No test covers either. A mutation that drops `context.action === 'publish' ||` or the draft
lookup goes unnoticed. If F01 is fixed through the schema, a single "publish an existing draft
with no coverage is refused" test still pins the behaviour. Asserting the Spanish message
(`'Un plan publicado necesita al menos una cobertura.'`) would also make each test fail for the
right reason.

### US-02-R1-F03 — The money formatter's options are untyped

`money-format.ts:15-21` casts the whole object through `unknown`, so a typo such as
`maximumFractionDigit: 0` or `style: 'curency'` would compile. The comment's reasoning is right:
the ES2022 typings lack `'always'`. But the fix is available. With
`tsc --target ES2022 --lib ES2022,ES2023.Intl`, `useGrouping: 'always'` type-checks with no
cast (reviewer's scratch check with the project's TypeScript 6.0.3). A narrower cast on the one
property would also keep the rest of the object checked. AC-06 is met; this is maintainability
only.

### US-02-R1-F04 — The secret-scan exclusion is wider than the log scan that replaces it

Assessment of orchestrator point 7: separating the code gate from the log scan is sound. The
log findings are classified once and recorded (23 of them), and mixing them into the gate would
hide a new code secret among accepted ones. Two gaps remain:
1. The exclusion and its replacement do not match. `case "$f" in logs/sessions/*) continue`
   drops `logs/sessions/README.md` and any non-jsonl file under `logs/sessions/`, while the
   documented log command is `git ls-files 'logs/sessions/*.jsonl'`. A secret pasted into the
   README (the file where findings are discussed) or into a `.txt`/`.md` export is checked by
   neither path. Narrowing the exclusion to `logs/sessions/*.jsonl` closes this.
2. The log scan is procedural only (`session-handoff`), and the "count must match" rule is
   checked by nobody. A mechanical check (for example, a recorded expected count that the script
   compares, or a `trace.sh`/gate step that runs the log scan against a baseline) would make it
   a control rather than a promise. This half can be justified as `won't fix` for this project
   size, if the human prefers.

### US-02-R1-F05 — Non-bisectable commits (orchestrator point 6)

Reproduced with `git archive 1491d73 frontend` and then `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json`:
`summary-step-guard.ts(4,27): error TS2307: Cannot find module './plan-store'`. The same holds at
`4f032ce`; `93ce8da` fixes it. Calibrated as a **nit**:
- The test-first flow already leaves `npm test` red from `56fa702` to the implementation by
  design, so bisecting this branch needs `git bisect skip` anyway.
- No rule requires every commit to build.
- It cannot be fixed without rewriting history, which §10 forbids on a pushed branch.

Suggested resolution: `won't fix`, with a lesson for the implementers (commit a module before
its first importer, and register a middleware in the commit that adds it).

`adr/README.md:37` says "ADR-0007, Proposed"; `:35` says "the orchestrator records acceptance"
(done: `adr/0007` has `status: Accepted`). `specs/README.md:18` says "next: ADR-0007".
`specs/US-02/tasks.md:13` (Blockers) still describes the pending acceptance, and the T-03..T-10
rows still say "written, red" although the tests are green. `FLOW.md:198` is an empty line
inside the "Where AI failed" table, so the new row at 199 renders as a loose paragraph of pipes.

`e266d9a test(backend): remove probe plans after each test…` changed `plan-rules.test.ts` after

### US-02-R1-F01 — Coverage middleware duplicates what the schema can enforce

Evidence: `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/services/entity-validator/index.js`:
- `addMinMax` (around lines 36-45) applies `.min(attr.min)` when
  `attr.required || (Array.isArray(value) && value.length > 0)`.
- For repeatable components, lines 98-109 call it whenever `!options.isDraft`.
- `document-service/entries.js:107-111,141-145` validate create and update with
  `isDraft: !data.publishedAt`, and `publishEntry` (`:159-197`) goes through `createEntry` with
  `publishedAt` set.

So with `"required": true` next to `"min": 1` on `coverages`, Strapi itself rejects `[]` on every
published write (create, update and publish), and drafts stay free. Today the attribute is not
`required`, so an empty array skips `min`. That is why the middleware works, but it is custom
code standing in for a one-word schema change. The comment at `plan-coverages.ts:7-9` ("never in
the Document Service") would also mislead the next maintainer.

Expected: either use the schema (and drop the middleware), or keep the middleware and correct
its comment with the reason the schema option was rejected (for example, an admin UX
difference). Both are acceptable. The human's rule is to keep bespoke backend code to a minimum.

### US-02-R1-F02 — Only the `create` branch of the coverage rule is tested

The test-engineer's note ("asserts that it rejects, not why") is **not** the real gap. The
control test "a plan with a country can be published" proves that the helper's data is otherwise
valid, and Strapi does not reject `[]` for a non-required repeatable (F01 evidence). So removing
the middleware turns the test red, even without a message assertion. The real gap is the other
branches of `plan-coverages.ts:18-25`:
- `publish` of an existing draft that has no coverages. This is the editor's normal path: save a
  draft, then publish.
- `update` with `status: 'published'` and no `coverages` in `data`, which goes through the draft
  lookup.

No test covers either. A mutation that drops `context.action === 'publish' ||` or the draft
lookup goes unnoticed. If F01 is fixed through the schema, a single "publish an existing draft
with no coverage is refused" test still pins the behaviour. Asserting the Spanish message

### US-02-R1-F01 — Coverage middleware duplicates what the schema can enforce

Evidence: `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/services/entity-validator/index.js`:
- `addMinMax` (around lines 36-45) applies `.min(attr.min)` when
  `attr.required || (Array.isArray(value) && value.length > 0)`.
- For repeatable components, lines 98-109 call it whenever `!options.isDraft`.
- `document-service/entries.js:107-111,141-145` validate create and update with
  `isDraft: !data.publishedAt`, and `publishEntry` (`:159-197`) goes through `createEntry` with
  `publishedAt` set.

So with `"required": true` next to `"min": 1` on `coverages`, Strapi itself rejects `[]` on every
published write (create, update and publish), and drafts stay free. Today the attribute is not
`required`, so an empty array skips `min`. That is why the middleware works, but it is custom
code standing in for a one-word schema change. The comment at `plan-coverages.ts:7-9` ("never in
the Document Service") would also mislead the next maintainer.

Expected: either use the schema (and drop the middleware), or keep the middleware and correct
its comment with the reason the schema option was rejected (for example, an admin UX
difference). Both are acceptable. The human's rule is to keep bespoke backend code to a minimum.

valid, and Strapi does not reject `[]` for a non-required repeatable (F01 evidence). So removing
the middleware turns the test red, even without a message assertion. The real gap is the other
branches of `plan-coverages.ts:18-25`:

  draft, then publish.
- `update` with `status: 'published'` and no `coverages` in `data`, which goes through the draft

lookup goes unnoticed. If F01 is fixed through the schema, a single "publish an existing draft
with no coverage is refused" test still pins the behaviour. Asserting the Spanish message
(`'Un plan publicado necesita al menos una cobertura.'`) would also make each test fail for the
right reason.

- `document-service/entries.js:107-111,141-145` validate create and update with
  `isDraft: !data.publishedAt`, and `publishEntry` (`:159-197`) goes through `createEntry` with
  `publishedAt` set.

So with `"required": true` next to `"min": 1` on `coverages`, Strapi itself rejects `[]` on every
published write (create, update and publish), and drafts stay free. Today the attribute is not
`required`, so an empty array skips `min`. That is why the middleware works, but it is custom
code standing in for a one-word schema change. The comment at `plan-coverages.ts:7-9` ("never in
the Document Service") would also mislead the next maintainer.

its comment with the reason the schema option was rejected (for example, an admin UX
difference). Both are acceptable. The human's rule is to keep bespoke backend code to a minimum.

I found no blocker or major findings. There are 4 minors to fix or justify before HC3, and 3 nits. Every automated AC has a passing test that I ran myself.

Report: /Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/reviews/US-02-review-R1.md (the only file I wrote; it is untracked). The `mci-review` stack is down with `-v`.

### Open findings
**Minor**
- **US-02-R1-F01** (`backend/src/documents/plan-coverages.ts:4-31`, `schema.json:49-54`): the "at least one coverage" middleware is custom code the schema can replace. In Strapi 5.63, if `coverages` were marked `required` next to `min: 1`, Strapi itself would refuse an empty list on create, update and publish (checked in `@strapi/core` `entity-validator/index.js` and `document-service/entries.js`). The middleware's comment says Strapi "never" does this, which is wrong. Rule: ADR-0007 D6 / ADR-0006 D4 (keep custom backend code to a minimum).
- **US-02-R1-F02** (`backend/tests/plan-rules.test.ts:238-240`): only the `create` path of the coverage rule is tested. Publishing an existing draft (the normal editor path) and updating with `status: 'published'` are not. Removing `context.action === 'publish'` from the middleware keeps every test green. On your point 4: the missing "why" assertion is **not** the real gap. The control test proves the test data is otherwise valid, and Strapi does not refuse an empty list for a non-required component, so removing the middleware would turn the test red.
- **US-02-R1-F03** (`frontend/src/app/shared/money-format.ts:15-21`): the cast through `unknown` turns off type checking for the whole options object. Adding `ES2023.Intl` to `lib` makes `useGrouping: 'always'` type-check with no cast (checked with the project's TypeScript 6.0.3).
- **US-02-R1-F04** (`scripts/scan-secrets.sh:42`): the gate now skips every file under `logs/sessions/`, but the separate log scan only covers `*.jsonl`. So `logs/sessions/README.md`, or any other non-jsonl file there, is checked by neither. The log scan is also a manual step that nothing enforces.

**Nit**
- **US-02-R1-F05**: the history cannot be bisected at two commits. `1491d73` and `4f032ce` fail `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json` with TS2307 for `./plan-store`. Also, `plan-coverages.ts` is added in `6786a72` but only registered in `84cfc51`. I suggest closing it as won't fix, since fixing it means rewriting history.
- **US-02-R1-F06**: several status lines are out of date:
  - `adr/README.md:35,37` still calls ADR-0007 Proposed.
  - `specs/README.md:18` still says "next: ADR-0007".
  - `specs/US-02/tasks.md:13` still lists the acceptance as a blocker, and rows 27-34 still say "written, red".
  - A blank line at `FLOW.md:198` cuts the new row off from its table.
- **US-02-R1-F07**: `e266d9a` changed a test during step 4, and nothing records which agent wrote it. The change itself is sound: it only moves cleanup to after each test, and no assertion changed.

### Your other points
- **Point 1, `PlanStore`**: correct. It is keyed by country, never caches failures or empty answers, so "Reintentar" asks again, and a new plan shows on the next full reload, which is what AC-12 requires. No finding.
- **Point 2, card accessibility**: works as intended. I checked it in a browser:
  - arrow keys move and choose, with wrap;
  - Tab order is the plan group, "Atrás", "Continuar";
  - each option is named by its plan name, and its description reads "Recomendado | description | price";
  - the radio shows a 3px focus outline, and after the z-index fix a click on the radio's centre reaches the radio;
  - "Recomendado" is text, not colour alone.

  For the HC3 screen-reader pass, check two announcements: the empty-state message, and that "Elige un plan para continuar." is heard once.
- **Point 3, prices**: no finding beyond F03. ADR-0007 is followed exactly (integer arithmetic, round half up, the injectable clock), and the factor values appear only in `price-rules.ts`.
- **Point 5, US-02-Q-10**: nothing is exposed beyond the accepted inactive-plan read.
- **Points 6 and 7**: see F05 and F04.

### Checks I ran
- **Frontend**: lint, tsc (app and spec) and build all exit 0; unit tests **590/590**.
- **Backend**: tsc, lint and build exit 0; tests **49/49**.
- **E2E** on a clean stack (`up --build --wait`):
  - full suite **78/78** (19.1 s), then **78/78** again (18.7 s);
  - the two US-02 files with `--repeat-each=5`: **190/190**, none flaky.
- **`scripts/trace.sh US-02`**: exit 0, no AC without a test (AC-18 is manual), no open blocker or major.
- **`scripts/trace.sh US-01`**: exit 0. The minor R4-F01 and nit R4-F02 are still open, as on `main`.
- **`scripts/scan-secrets.sh`** (full output read): exit 0, 262 files. All 6 allowed exceptions were already there. The one new marker sits on a line no rule matches, so it does nothing.
- **Security probes on :1337 and :8080**, using one admin login, then the four e2e runs:
  - No draft (`joven`, `flex`) came back for any of these: `status=draft`, `DRAFT`, `status[0]`, `publicationState=preview`, `hasPublishedVersion=false`, the paths `/API`, `/Api`, `/api/Plans` and trailing slash, or non-Bearer Authorization headers (the proxy answers 400 to any Authorization header). No row came back with a null `publishedAt`.
  - Writes are refused: POST, PUT and DELETE get 403 on Strapi; POST gets 405 on the proxy.
  - `findOne` gets 403 on Strapi and 404 on the proxy.
  - `populate[createdBy]` and filters on it get 400.
  - A token with only `country.find` gets 403 on plans and form fields.
  - Side note, not new in US-02: that token can read country drafts with `status=draft`. This is the existing ADR-0002 behaviour.

### AC verification
- AC-01 to AC-17 and AC-19 are implemented, and each has passing unit, component or e2e tests. AC-15 is covered at all three levels.
- AC-18 is manual by design; I confirmed there is no horizontal scroll at 360 and 1280 px.
- Still to check by hand at HC3: the second scenario of AC-08 and the admin part of AC-12 (both T-22), the recommended visual style, and the screen-reader pass.
- The US-01 hand-over items pass in `us-01-03-full-flow-co.spec.ts`: US-01-AC-04, AC-18, AC-20, the first scenario of AC-21, and the step 2 heading focus of AC-24.
